title: Behavior of higher-order MDD on energy ratios at the interface of thermoelastic and piezothermoelastic mediums
research_objective: Investigate energy distribution at interface between thermoelastic (TS) and piezothermoelastic with MDD/TPL (HPS) half-spaces; analyze effect of higher-order MDD parameters (n,p,l) on energy ratios
novel_contribution: Energy ratios computed for reflected/transmitted waves at piezothermoelastic-thermoelastic interface with higher-order MDD; three models compared (n=4,p=3,l=3; n=3,p=2,l=2; n=p=l=1); 25 figures; conservation claimed (sum ≈ 1)
physical_model: Orthotropic piezothermoelastic half-space (HPS, x3>0) with TPL + higher-order MDD; thermoelastic half-space (TS, x3<0); welded interface at x3=0; 2D plane strain (x1-x3 plane)
dimensionality: Linear continuum; small deformations; harmonic plane waves; absence of free charge, body forces, shear forces; no inertial terms in electric equation; engineering notation with dot/subscript
mathematical_assumptions: Eqs (3)-(8): constitutive, momentum, electric field, electric displacement, charge conservation, heat conduction with TPL+MDD; Eqs (12)-(15): 2D HPS governing equations; Eqs (21)-(23): TS governing equations; Eqs (31)-(33): TS potential formulation
governing_equations: Eq (3): σ_ij = c_ijro e_ro - η_ijr E_r - β_ij T; Eq (6): D_i = ε_ij E_j + η_ijr e_jr + p_i T; Eq (8): heat conduction with D_τ_T^m, D_τ_v^m, D_τ_q^m operators
constitutive_relations: Piezo-thermo-elastic coupling (η_ijr, p_i); thermal-electric coupling (p_i T in D_i); electrical boundary condition D_3 = 0
coupling_terms: Eq (27): G_11 q^8 + G_12 q^6 + G_13 q^4 + G_14 q^2 + G_15 = 0 (8th-order characteristic equation; roots q_1-q_4 positive imaginary, q_5-q_8 negative imaginary)
boundary_interface_conditions: Eq (24): (u_1,u_3,φ,T) = (H,M,N,U) exp[iω(-x_1/c - q x_3 + t)]; Eq (34): TS potential form (φ^e,T^e,ψ^e) = (A_φe,A_Te,A_ψe) exp[ik(-x_1 sinθ_0 - x_3 cosθ_0) + iωt]
wave_solution_ansatz: Eq (27): det(Ω) = 0 → 8th-order polynomial in q; Eq (35): TS roots r_e1^2, r_e2^2, r_e3^2 = α_2*²
secular_equation: Not explicitly given as separate formula; energy ratios derived from flux expressions
energy_density_formulation: Eq (45): P = -Re(σ_13 u̇_1_bar + σ_33 u̇_3_bar - φ Ḋ_3_bar + K_3 T̄_3 T/T_0) [HPS side - includes mechanical + electrical + thermal]; Eq (46): P^e = -Re(σ_31^e u̇_1^e_bar + σ_33^e u̇_3^e_bar) [TS side - mechanical ONLY, NO thermal flux term]
energy_flux_definition: Eq (54)-(56): E_RP = <P_RP^e>/<P_IP^e>, etc.; amplitude ratios X_i = H_i/A* from Eq (44)
reflection_coefficient_definition: Energy fluxes from Eq (45)-(46); ratios from Eq (54)-(56)
transmission_coefficient_definition: Eq (54)-(56): energy ratios E_RP, E_RT, E_RS, ES_s (s=1-4); interaction energy E_st (Eq 57); conservation Eq (58): Σ(ES_s + E_int + E_RP + E_RT + E_RS) = 1
main_analytical_results: MATLAB; roots of characteristic equation solved numerically
numerical_methods: TS: magnesium; HPS: cadmium selenide (parameters from Mondal & Othman 2021, Kumar & Sarthi 2006)
material_parameters: MATLAB numerical solution; graphical verification (25 figures)
validation_method: 11 limiting cases mapped: Case 1=Biot, Case 2=LS, Case 3=higher-order MDD, Case 4=GN-II, Case 5=GN-III, Case 6=Tzou DPL, Case 7=Ezzat et al., Case 8=Abouelregal DPL+MDD, Case 9=Roy Choudhuri TPL, Case 10=Ghosh et al., Case 11=Abouelregal higher-order TPL
limiting_case_checks: Claimed: 'total of energy ratios is almost equal to one at each angle'; BUT energy flux definitions are ASYMMETRIC - TS side (Eq 46) omits thermal heat flux term while HPS side (Eq 45) includes K_3 T̄_3 T/T_0 thermal conduction term
energy_balance_checks: Kernel function κ(t-ζ) choices; phase lag times τ_q=0.05s, τ_T=0.03s, τ_v=0.02s; Chiriţă et al. stability: n≥5 or p≥5 leads to unstable system; Quintanilla & Racke 2008 stability conditions
thermodynamic_admissibility: 1. ASYMMETRIC ENERGY FLUX: TS medium energy flux (Eq 46) excludes thermal conduction term that HPS medium includes (Eq 45) - claimed conservation (Eq 58) may not hold for total energy; 2. No explicit energy density formulation given; 3. Interaction energy terms (E_st) included between refracted waves but physical interpretation unclear; 4. Electrical boundary D_3=0 (insulated) is a specific choice, not general
scientific_weaknesses: 1. Verify whether Σ energy ratios = 1 holds when thermal flux is included on BOTH sides; 2. Derive proper total energy flux for TS medium including thermal transport; 3. Test conservation with asymmetric flux definitions; 4. Investigate whether interaction energy terms E_st represent physical energy exchange or mathematical artifacts
open_research_problems: Eqs (1)-(58) as numbered in source; Section 'Energy ratios' (Eqs 45-58); Section 'Limiting cases' (Cases 1-11)
